fair_value_reason: 60% weight on 14x a ~$19.2 NTM EPS at Sep-2027 (2027 consensus $18.10 rolled forward with a small cycle haircut) = ~$269, and 40% on ~$15 of 2027 FCF per share (24% margin on ~$15.9B revenue, ~252M shares) at a 6% yield = ~$250. Blended, ~$262. This equals the round-2 agent mean ($262.2). No agent's inputs needed correcting this round: share count, EPS base, net debt and multiples are now consistent across all five. It is down from my round-1 $265 because four of five agents tightened multiples and yields for the Sep 16 hike.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged: all five now use ~14x a ~$19 NTM EPS because of the Sep 16 Fed hike, fair values sit at $253-271 (mean $262), and P(close >= $236) is 0.50-0.56. My fact-checks confirmed agent_1's new sell-in flag (distributor revenue +26.7% y/y against +9.4% direct, 59% of sales, 10-Q). They found the NXP September price round is single-sourced and the sector-pricing figures are ST data relayed by a Substack. They also confirmed agent_5's base rates: analog semis rose in 12 months after a first hike in 7 of 8 cases, and NXPI's 12-month dispersion is 0.23-0.29. I keep the median near $247-250 and fair value at $262, and narrow the distribution slightly to ~41% effective sigma, mostly in the left tail. The Oct 27 print (watch distributor weeks) and the Oct 28 FOMC are the near-term binaries.
key_drivers: Fundamentals are still accelerating: Q2 revenue was $3.50B (+19.5% y/y) and the Q3 guide is $3.75B / $4.11 EPS. 2027 consensus EPS of $18.10 is rising ($17.71 a month ago), so the stock trades at ~13x.

Sell-in is the main risk, not China alone. Distributor revenue grew +26.7% y/y against +9.4% for direct sales and is 59% of revenue (10-Q), and channel inventory is 11 weeks against 9. Watch both in the Oct 27 print.

Pricing power is sector-wide (ST's third 2026 increase, TI, Infineon; lead times of 40-52 weeks), and NXP says its pricing builds into 2027. A third NXP round in September is reported by only one source.

Rates cap the multiple: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and meets on Oct 28. All five agents now use ~14x. After past first hikes, analog semis still rose over the next 12 months in 7 of 8 cases.
Volatility is high but mean-reverting: realized is 47-52% now, while 12-month dispersion has historically been 0.23-0.29, so an effective ~41% is the reconciled width.
